Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1234 PM CDT Thu Aug 06 2026

Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS IN PARTS OF THE
MID-MISSOURI VALLEY INTO WISCONSIN AND THE UPPER PENINSULA OF
MICHIGAN...PARTS OF THE NORTHERN MID-ATLANTIC...SOUTH-CENTRAL SOUTH
DAKOTA INTO NORTH-CENTRAL NEBRASKA...

...SUMMARY...
A few strong to severe storms may occur from the Mid-Missouri Valley
across Wisconsin and into Upper Michigan Friday, with areas of
strong/damaging wind gusts and isolated marginal hail. Other storms
may produce locally damaging gusts over parts of the Northeast and
hail over parts of central Nebraska/South Dakota.

...Mid-Missouri Valley into Wisconsin/Upper Peninsular Michigan...
A cold front will move into the Upper Midwest during the afternoon.
Moisture return ahead of the front will maintain upper 60s F farther
north to low 70s F dewpoints across Iowa/southern Minnesota.
2000-3000 J/kg MLCAPE is expected during the afternoon. The
approaching mid-level jet will bring stronger mid-level flow and
30-45 kt of effective shear to the region (stronger shear will
generally exist with southwestward extent). Initial activity will
likely be cellular with a tendency to become more linear with time.
Large hail and damaging winds will be the main concerns. Given the
stronger buoyancy and shear within Iowa, there is greater potential
for an MCS to develop with an associated greater risk for wind
damage. Variance is relatively high within model guidance as to
where this corridor will exist due in part to the subtle forcing.
Some guidance suggests a cluster of activity is possible during the
morning hours. This could intensify as the airmass destabilizes
during the day. Other guidance suggests limited morning activity
with storms forming along the front farther east. An increase in
wind probabilities is possible as confidence increases.

...South Dakota/Nebraska...
At least moderate elevated instability is forecast to develop as a
low-level jet intensifies within the region late Friday night into
early Saturday morning. Several CAMs and global guidance suggest
development will occur. Sufficient mid-level flow on the southern
flank of the northern Plains trough will allow for organized storms.
Steep mid-level lapse rates will support a risk for isolated large
hail.

...Northern Mid-Atlantic...
Though mid-level winds will be slightly weaker than on Thursday, the
approach of a modest trough will allow for marginally organized
storms within a very moist environment. Afternoon MLCAPE will near
2000 J/kg in parts of the Mid-Atlantic. Model consensus continues to
support the potential for widely scattered to scattered storms
within this weakly capped airmass. Isolated damaging winds will be
possible.

...Southern Plains into the Ozarks...
Given the presence of a stalled boundary/outflow, some potential
exists for storms to develop during the afternoon. Confidence on
where this boundary will be placed is quite low at this time.
Deep-layer shear will also be somewhat weak as well. Given these
factors, severe wind probabilities will be withheld, though isolated
wind damage could occur.

..Wendt.. 08/06/2026

$$

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0231 PM CDT Thu Aug 06 2026

Valid 081200Z - 091200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM PARTS OF
CENTRAL SOUTH DAKOTA/NEBRASKA INTO IOWA AND NORTHERN MISSOURI...

...SUMMARY...
A corridor of damaging winds may develop Saturday afternoon and
evening from South Dakota/Nebraska into Iowa/Northern Missouri.

...South Dakota/Nebraska into Mid-Missouri/Mississippi Valleys...
Models are in general agreement that convection will be ongoing
early Saturday morning near the central South Dakota/Nebraska
border. There is some potential for this activity to intensify as
destabilization occurs in eastern Nebraska into Iowa during the
afternoon. Moderate mid-level flow will extend into these regions.
Strong heating to the south of a developing warm front/outflow
boundary will lead to a strongly unstable environment. The two main
questions for this forecast will be whether the early morning
activity can develop enough of a cold pool to persist through the
diurnally unfavorable morning time frame, and what the impacts from
potential convection in Iowa on Friday will be. The overall setup
and environment appear favorable for MCS development. Higher
probabilities will likely be needed as confidence in the corridor of
greater risk increases.

...Mid-Atlantic...
Some potential for thunderstorms exists during the afternoon as a
very moist and uncapped airmass will remain in place on Saturday.
Mid-level flow will be stronger with northern extent with cyclonic
flow aloft continuing over the Great Lakes/New England. Though
widely scattered to scattered storms are probable, effective shear
and mid-level lapse rates will be weak. Furthermore, mesoscale
features aiding convective organization are not evident in model
guidance. There may be an embedded perturbation within the flow
aloft, but models differ on the location/intensity of these
features. Uncertainty in storm severity remains high.

..Wendt.. 08/06/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0300 AM CDT Thu Aug 06 2026

Valid 091200Z - 141200Z

...DISCUSSION...
For the Sunday/D4 through Thursday/D8 period, an elongated zone of
thunderstorm/wind potential will exist from the northern Plains
across parts of the Midwest/Great Lakes, and possibly extending into
parts of the Northeast. Predictability is low for this pattern given
the likelihood of ongoing corridors of storms early each day, and
variability with the position of the elongated west to east front.
However, the presence of a very moist air mass, with possibly strong
instability to the south, combined with possible waves rotating
around the large-scale upper trough over Canada, may yield storm
corridors with damaging wind potential. One or more areas may be
denoted in later outlooks as the events near in time.

At this time, rough areas of interest include the northern Plains to
Upper Midwest on Sunday/D4, and portions of the Great Lakes/Midwest
on Monday/D5.

..Jewell.. 08/06/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1251 AM CDT Fri Aug 07 2026

Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PARTS OF THE
MID-ATLANTIC...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated to scattered strong to severe thunderstorms capable of
producing damaging winds are expected across portions of the
Mid-Atlantic this afternoon. More isolated severe thunderstorms are
expected from the mid-Missouri Valley into the Lake Superior region
as well as across parts of the southern High Plains and central
Plains.

...Synopsis...
00 UTC upper-air analyses and latest GOES water-vapor imagery depict
several perturbations within a low-amplitude upper trough in place
over the central CONUS. The first of these perturbations is analyzed
over the mid-MS Valley and is expected to migrate east towards the
Mid-Atlantic region by mid-afternoon. A more pronounced shortwave
trough is evident over central Canada into the northern Plains. This
feature, along with an attendant surface low and trailing cold
front, will move eastward through the day, reaching the Great Lakes
region by tonight. Strong to severe thunderstorm chances will
primarily be associated with these synoptic features, though more
localized corridors of strong/severe thunderstorms may emerge across
the southern High Plains and parts of the Ozarks associated with
outflow boundaries from ongoing convection. 

...Mid-Atlantic...
The weak upper perturbation currently over the MS Valley is forecast
to reach the central Appalachians/Mid-Atlantic region by
mid-afternoon. Strong heating of an seasonally moist air mass
(dewpoints in the low to mid 70s) will compensate for otherwise
meager mid-level lapse rates and support MLCAPE values of 1000-2000
J/kg with minimal capping by early afternoon. A combination of weak
synoptic lift aided by localized orographic ascent should promote
isolated to scattered thunderstorm development during the 18-20 UTC
period. Most CAM guidance depicts a reasonably strong signal for
thunderstorm clustering and upscale growth as storms spread
northeast towards the I-95 corridor around peak heating. Although
winds through the lowest 2-3 km will remain fairly modest, steep
low-level lapse rates and around 25 knots of effective bulk shear
should promote loosely organized clusters/lines with embedded swaths
of damaging winds. 
 
...Mid-Missouri Valley into the Lake Superior region...
Thunderstorm development along the cold front is expected early this
morning, possibly as early as 12-14 UTC across portions of eastern
MN. This early activity will likely be elevated in nature, but 30-35
knot mid-level flow should support adequate hodograph elongation for
a few organized cells capable of severe hail. With time, diurnal
heating/destabilization downstream and persistent forcing along the
front should promote steady intensification and upscale growth of
convection with a transition to primarily a wind risk across WI and
the Upper Peninsula of MI. Further south, more isolated thunderstorm
coverage across southern MN, IA, and eastern NE may support a
supercell or two with an attendant threat for large hail as well as
severe wind. 

...Southern High Plains into the Ozarks...
Isolated thunderstorms are expected to develop across northeast NM
into the TX Panhandle this afternoon - driven by either orographic
ascent along the Sange de Cristo mountains and/or the Raton Mesa or
lift along a residual outflow boundary associated with an ongoing,
but fairly confined, MCS across the northern TX Panhandle (as of 06
UTC). Regardless of the forcing mechanism, convection developing
across this region will mature in an environment featuring fairly
weak wind shear, but a deeply-mixed boundary layer conducive for
severe downbursts. Despite considerable variance in storm placement
and coverage in latest CAM ensembles, the consistent signal for
severe downbursts warrants low-end severe wind probabilities. 

Further east into eastern OK and the Ozarks, a focused corridor of
thunderstorms will likely emerge on the outflow boundary of a
convective cluster developing across eastern KS (as of 06 UTC). Some
CAM solutions hint that sporadic large hail and/or damaging
downbursts will be possible with this activity, but considerable
uncertainty on where and how intense this activity will be limits
confidence on introducing additional risk areas. 

...Nebraska/South Dakota...
Elevated convection is expected to develop across portions of
northern NE and southern SD during the overnight hours tonight as
isentropic ascent increases in tandem with a modest intensification
of a low-level jet.  Low-level moistening through 850 mb under a
plume of 7-8 C/km mid-level lapse rates should promote a adequate
buoyancy few robust updrafts (though confidence in storm coverage is
limited due to the weak nature of the forcing for ascent). However,
strong shear across the region will likely promote organized
convection, including a supercell or two, capable of producing large
hail.

..Moore/Marsh.. 08/07/2026
